# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 7

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 28

---

## Disagreement 001 — v. 1: Instruments of compulsion

- **EMET:** "under torture with whips and cords"
- **LOGOS:** "by means of whips and scourges"
- **PNEUMA:** "with whips and leather cords"
- **Note:** Greek *mastixin kai neurophinais* — whips and sinew-cords/scourges. "Cords" (EMET) is most literal; "scourges" (LOGOS) is the conventional term; PNEUMA specifies "leather." SOPHIA uses "whips and scourges."

## Disagreement 002 — v. 2: The spokesman's challenge

- **EMET:** "What do you intend to ask and learn from us?"
- **LOGOS:** "What do you intend to ask of us and find out?"
- **PNEUMA:** "What are you trying to find out by doing this to us?"
- **Note:** PNEUMA shifts the emphasis to the torture itself ("by doing this"). EMET/LOGOS follow the Greek more closely. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 003 — v. 3: King's anger

- **EMET:** "The king fell into a rage"
- **LOGOS:** "The king was infuriated"
- **PNEUMA:** "The king exploded with fury"
- **Note:** Greek *pikranthe ho basileus*. "Fell into a rage" (EMET) is idiomatic; "infuriated" (LOGOS) is clean; "exploded" (PNEUMA) is vivid but idiomatic. SOPHIA uses "was enraged."

## Disagreement 004 — v. 5: "the fumes/smoke spread"

- **EMET:** "as the smoke from the pan spread widely"
- **LOGOS:** "while the fumes from the pan spread everywhere"
- **PNEUMA:** "The smoke rolled up and spread through the room"
- **Note:** Greek *en tō diapeiresthai ton kapnon*. "Widely" (EMET) vs. "everywhere" (LOGOS) vs. "through the room" (PNEUMA — adds "room," not in Greek). SOPHIA uses "far and wide."

## Disagreement 005 — v. 6: "truly has compassion"

- **EMET:** "in truth has compassion on us"
- **LOGOS:** "he truly has compassion on us"
- **PNEUMA:** "He truly has compassion on us"
- **Note:** LOGOS and PNEUMA agree. EMET's "in truth" is slightly more formal. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 006 — v. 7: Scalping description

- **EMET:** "tearing off the skin of his head with the hair"
- **LOGOS:** "after tearing off the skin of his head along with the hair"
- **PNEUMA:** "They tore the scalp from his head, hair and all"
- **Note:** PNEUMA uses "scalp" — an accurate and vivid term. LOGOS is formally equivalent to the Greek. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 007 — v. 9: "King of the universe"

- **EMET:** "the King of the universe will raise us up"
- **LOGOS:** "the King of the universe will raise us up"
- **PNEUMA:** "the King of the universe will raise us up"
- **Note:** All three agents agree on this crucial phrase. Greek *ho tou kosmou basileus*. Noted for agreement.

## Disagreement 008 — v. 9: "everlasting renewal of life"

- **EMET:** "to an everlasting renewal of life"
- **LOGOS:** "to an everlasting renewal of life"
- **PNEUMA:** "to a life renewed forever"
- **Note:** Greek *anabiōsin aiōnion* — eternal coming-back-to-life. EMET and LOGOS agree on "everlasting renewal of life." PNEUMA's "life renewed forever" slightly inverts. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.

## Disagreement 009 — v. 11: Hands and tongue

- **EMET:** "I got these from Heaven, and because of his laws I disdain them"
- **LOGOS:** "These I received from Heaven, and for the sake of his laws I disdain them"
- **PNEUMA:** "'These came to me from Heaven,' he said calmly. 'For the sake of his laws I hold them cheap.'"
- **Note:** "Disdain" vs. "hold them cheap" vs. implicit "disdain." LOGOS's "received" vs. EMET's "got." SOPHIA uses "I received these from Heaven, and for the sake of his laws I hold them cheap."

## Disagreement 010 — v. 12: King's reaction

- **EMET:** "struck with amazement at the young man's spirit, for he regarded his sufferings as nothing"
- **LOGOS:** "struck with amazement at the spirit of the young man, for he made nothing of his sufferings"
- **PNEUMA:** "The king and his court stared at the young man in disbelief. He simply did not seem to feel what was happening to him."
- **Note:** PNEUMA significantly paraphrases and changes "king and those with him" to "king and his court." LOGOS is more precise. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 011 — v. 14: Resurrection asymmetry

- **EMET:** "But for you there will be no resurrection to life"
- **LOGOS:** "But for you there will be no resurrection to life"
- **PNEUMA:** "For you — there is no resurrection. None."
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree exactly. PNEUMA adds "None" for rhetorical weight. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS; the Greek stands without elaboration.

## Disagreement 012 — v. 16: Power statement

- **EMET:** "you have authority among men, mortal though you are"
- **LOGOS:** "you have authority over human beings, mortal as you are"
- **PNEUMA:** "You have power over human beings because you are a man among men"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "because you are a man among men" introduces a different logic than the Greek *su men phthartos ōn* — you being mortal. The point is that his authority is limited by mortality. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 013 — v. 17: Threat to descendants

- **EMET:** "how he will torment you and your descendants"
- **LOGOS:** "how he will torment you and your descendants"
- **PNEUMA:** "when he brings his torment down on you and on your children"
- **Note:** "Children" (PNEUMA) vs. "descendants" (EMET/LOGOS) for Greek *sperma* — seed/offspring. "Descendants" is more literal. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.

## Disagreement 014 — v. 18: "things worthy of wonder/astonishment"

- **EMET:** "things worthy of wonder have happened to us"
- **LOGOS:** "things worthy of astonishment have come upon us"
- **PNEUMA:** "it is astonishing and right"
- **Note:** Greek *paradoxa* — astonishing/paradoxical things. EMET "wonder," LOGOS "astonishment." SOPHIA uses "astonishment."

## Disagreement 015 — v. 20: Mother's courage

- **EMET:** "bore it with good courage because of her hope in the LORD"
- **LOGOS:** "she bore it with courage because of her hope in the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "she endured it with courage because she hoped in the LORD"
- **Note:** "Good courage" (EMET) vs. "courage" (LOGOS) — Greek *gennaios* is included in EMET. SOPHIA uses "bore it with good courage."

## Disagreement 016 — v. 21: "womanly feeling with man's courage"

- **EMET:** "reinforced her woman's reasoning with a man's courage"
- **LOGOS:** "reinforced her womanly feeling with a man's courage"
- **PNEUMA:** "charged her woman's tenderness with a man's courage"
- **Note:** Greek *thelukē logismō* — womanly reasoning/logic. "Reasoning" (EMET) is most literal; "feeling" (LOGOS) interprets; "tenderness" (PNEUMA) interprets further. SOPHIA uses "womanly feeling."

## Disagreement 017 — v. 22: Creator's act

- **EMET:** "nor I who set in order the elements within each of you"
- **LOGOS:** "nor I who arranged the elements that make up each of you"
- **PNEUMA:** "I did not compose from nothing the elements that make up each of you"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "from nothing" — an interpretive insertion anticipating v. 28. The Greek *tēn stoicheion... diekosmēsen* has no "from nothing" here. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 018 — v. 23: Key resurrection promise

- **EMET:** "will in his mercy give life and breath back to you again, since you now forget yourselves for the sake of his laws"
- **LOGOS:** "will in his mercy give life and breath back to you again — since you now hold your own lives cheap for the sake of his laws"
- **PNEUMA:** "in his mercy, he will give you back your life and your breath. Because you are now giving up those lives for his laws"
- **Note:** "Forget yourselves" (EMET) vs. "hold your own lives cheap" (LOGOS) vs. "giving up those lives" (PNEUMA). Greek *oligōrounta* — making light of, caring nothing for. SOPHIA uses LOGOS.

## Disagreement 019 — v. 27: The mother's deception of the tyrant

- **EMET:** "fooling the cruel tyrant"
- **LOGOS:** "mocking the cruel tyrant"
- **PNEUMA:** "and what she said was the opposite of what the tyrant expected"
- **Note:** Greek *ton ōmō tyranno apateōsa* — deceiving/tricking the cruel tyrant. "Fooling" (EMET) and "mocking" (LOGOS) both work; PNEUMA expands into explanation. SOPHIA uses "mocking."

## Disagreement 020 — v. 28: CREATION EX NIHILO — critical verse

- **EMET:** "God did not make them out of things that existed. And in the same way the human race came into being"
- **LOGOS:** "God did not make them out of things that existed. And in the same way the human race came into being"
- **PNEUMA:** "God did not make any of it from things that already existed. And that is how human beings came to exist too"
- **Note:** All three agents agree on the substance of the creation ex nihilo statement. PNEUMA adds "already" for emphasis. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS exactly, recognizing the theological primacy of this verse.

## Disagreement 021 — v. 29: Mother's promise

- **EMET:** "in God's mercy I may get you back again along with your brothers"
- **LOGOS:** "by God's mercy I may receive you back along with your brothers"
- **PNEUMA:** "God in his mercy will give you back to me — you and your brothers together"
- **Note:** PNEUMA separates "you and your brothers" for emphasis. LOGOS/EMET are more compact. SOPHIA uses LOGOS.

## Disagreement 022 — v. 34: Addressing Antiochus directly

- **EMET:** "unholy wretch, the most vile of all men"
- **LOGOS:** "unholy man, you most defiled of all people"
- **PNEUMA:** "you wretched, filthy man, the lowest creature breathing"
- **Note:** Greek *anosiōtate...pantōn anthrōpōn rhyparōtate* — most unholy... most defiled of all men. EMET is strong; LOGOS is accurate; PNEUMA's "lowest creature breathing" is an interpretive intensification. SOPHIA uses "unholy wretch, most vile of all men."

## Disagreement 023 — v. 36: "drunk of ever-flowing life"

- **EMET:** "have drunk of ever-flowing life, under God's covenant"
- **LOGOS:** "have now drunk of ever-flowing life under God's covenant"
- **PNEUMA:** "have now passed into everlasting life under God's covenant"
- **Note:** Greek *aenaou zōēs pepōkasin* — have drunk of ever-flowing life. "Drunk of" is a striking image — life as something consumed. PNEUMA substitutes "passed into," losing the drinking metaphor. SOPHIA preserves "drunk of ever-flowing life."

## Disagreement 024 — v. 37: "surrender body and soul"

- **EMET:** "give up body and life for the laws of our fathers"
- **LOGOS:** "surrender body and soul for the laws of our fathers"
- **PNEUMA:** "I give my body and my life for the laws of our fathers"
- **Note:** "Soul" (LOGOS) vs. "life" (EMET/PNEUMA) for Greek *psychēn*. In this resurrection context, "soul" is theologically preferable — the self continues beyond bodily death. SOPHIA uses "body and soul."

## Disagreement 025 — v. 37: Prayer for the nation

- **EMET:** "appealing to God to show mercy soon to our nation and by trials and plagues to make you confess that he alone is God"
- **LOGOS:** "I call upon God to show favor quickly to our nation, and through trials and plagues to bring you to confess that he alone is God"
- **PNEUMA:** "I call on God: let him act quickly to show mercy to our nation. Through suffering and plagues let him bring you to confess that he alone is God"
- **Note:** All three convey the intercession accurately. LOGOS and PNEUMA agree on "bring you to confess." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 026 — v. 39: King's fury

- **EMET:** "The king fell into a rage and handled him worse than the others, being exasperated at his scorn"
- **LOGOS:** "The king, enraged and inflamed by the young man's contemptuous tone, treated him more savagely than all the others"
- **PNEUMA:** "The king's rage boiled over. He treated the seventh brother more savagely than the rest — contempt was something Antiochus could not bear"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "contempt was something Antiochus could not bear" — an interpretive editorial. LOGOS is clean and accurate. SOPHIA uses LOGOS.

## Disagreement 027 — v. 40: "died undefiled"

- **EMET:** "died undefiled, putting his whole trust in the LORD"
- **LOGOS:** "died undefiled, trusting completely in the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "So the boy died too, pure to the last, with absolute trust in the LORD"
- **Note:** "Pure to the last" (PNEUMA) for *amiantos* — undefiled/unpolluted. EMET and LOGOS agree on "undefiled." SOPHIA uses "undefiled, trusting completely in the LORD."

## Disagreement 028 — v. 41: Mother's death

- **EMET:** "Last of all, the mother died, after her sons"
- **LOGOS:** "Last of all, after her sons, the mother died"
- **PNEUMA:** "After her sons, the mother died"
- **Note:** PNEUMA omits "last of all." The Greek *de teleutaia tōn hyiōn hē mētēr apeithanen* — but last of the sons the mother died. SOPHIA uses: "Last of all, after her sons, the mother died." The placement of "last of all" matters — she outlasted every one of her children.
